correctness.rationale: From the exact sampled coefficient and a bounded Volterra input-output operator, the pathwise minimizer is Φ(W_h). Bounded second Frechet derivatives, the exact rank-one sensitivity factorization and independent-sign Hilbert-space triangular-array CLT yield the Gaussian law. Doob fourth-moment estimates give O(h) norm mean bias and negligible quadratic remainder; exact second moments of the linearized sum give C_T. The deterministic objective has Hessian H and exact regret identity, giving R_T. Positivity of the Dirichlet–Robin Green function proves x(r)>0 and G_r not zero, so both constants strictly positive. The embedded numeric checker validates derivative algebra and quadrature without substituting for analysis.

value.rationale: Unlike a generic O(sqrt(h)) upper control-error rate, a nonzero covariance, an exactly sharp expected squared-error asymptotic and an operational true-objective regret coefficient quantify the statistical cost of independently sampled dissipative time-splitting. These terms permit principled error budgets and distinguish bias from fluctuations for a canonical original-method specialization. The finding does not pretend to generalize to general matrices or adapted policies.
